title: NEB Class 12 Physics — Electrostatics — 2021
origin: curated NEB-pattern set for class-12 electrostatics

questions.question: State Coulomb's law in vector form. Two point charges $+4\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ and $-2\,\mu\mathrm{C}$ are $30\,\mathrm{cm}$ apart in air. Find the magnitude and nature of the force between them.
questions.solution:
Coulomb's law: $\vec{F}_{12} = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}\,\hat{r}_{12}$ — the force acts along the line joining the charges, repulsive for like signs and attractive for unlike signs.
Magnitude: $F = 9\times10^9 \times \frac{(4\times10^{-6})(2\times10^{-6})}{(0.3)^2} = 9\times10^9 \times \frac{8\times10^{-12}}{0.09} = \frac{72\times10^{-3}}{0.09} = 0.8\,\mathrm{N}$. The charges have opposite signs, so the force is attractive — each charge is pulled toward the other.

questions.question: Define electric field intensity and electric potential. Derive the relation $E = -dV/dr$ for a radial field and explain what the negative sign means.
questions.solution:
Field intensity $\vec{E} = \vec{F}/q_0$ is the force per unit positive test charge; potential $V = W/q_0$ is the work per unit charge to bring a test charge from infinity.
Moving a charge $q_0$ outward by $dr$ against the field needs work $dW = -q_0 E\,dr$ (field does $-E\,dr$ per unit charge), so $dV = -E\,dr$, i.e. $E = -dV/dr$.
The negative sign means the field points down the potential slope: from high potential toward low potential, exactly as a ball rolls downhill.

questions.question: A parallel-plate capacitor has capacitance $C_0$ with air between its plates. A dielectric slab of constant $K = 3$ is fully inserted. What is the new capacitance, and what happens to the stored energy if the capacitor is isolated (charge fixed)?
questions.solution:
Capacitance scales with the dielectric constant: $C = K C_0 = 3C_0$.
Isolated means charge $Q$ is fixed. Stored energy $U = Q^2/2C$ falls to one-third ($U = U_0/3$) because $C$ tripled. The 'missing' energy does work pulling the slab in — the field does work on the dielectric.
